findings.reason: as written, a coordinator sizes and briefs s4 believing the run eats into the failed drain's pending documentation, while the run can only touch 5 documentation-missing sources and the done-when cannot show the backlog moved, leaving 976 names and a 340-name documentation regression with no owning section.
findings.text: s4 states "The documentation backlog may still be open when the run starts; its classes are among those the run advances", but the backlog the drain actually left is a name-level one: `sib-docs-drain-after-admission` (commit 7aef43b21) records documentation stages after its stalled run as accepted 2,028, reviewed 46, drafted 3, pending 926, exhausted 1, with accepted documentation falling 340 net, whereas the census class s4 can advance for documentation is "documentation missing" at 5 sources (because the run is scoped by source), and s4's done-when measures no documentation stage at all — so the sentence promises progress on a 976-name backlog that nothing in the plan measures or owns.

findings.reason: the exclusion is unambiguous in effect for this run and the done-when does not require any vocabulary-gap source, so the ambiguity costs a reader one lookup rather than sending the run down a wrong path.
findings.text: s4 excludes the vocabulary-gap class "until the ISN release carrying its tokens is pinned" but names no such release or section, while §1 already records ISN 0.11.1 as "published and pinned" and the census still classes 92 sources at vocabulary gap, so the exclusion's stated exit condition reads as already satisfied and the only release identifier for the gap tokens (`imas-standard-names:dd-gap-vocabulary#s4`) lives in the sibling plan rather than here.

response_events.note: §4 no longer claims the run advances the drain's backlog; a new §5 owns the documentation backlog the stalled drain left, measured on the documentation stage of every live name.
